title: Acknowledgement (ZIFFER-SPEC-001 DR-4 / DR-5 / DR-9; ACK-1..ACK-6, reference-level)
description:
A signed acknowledgement of a floor-HIGH action being held for release. Carried on legs F5.4 and F5.5 of the leg register (ZIFFER-DEPLOY-001 Annex A): F5.4 is the DR-9 positive acknowledgement that releases an IRREVERSIBLE action, F5.5 is the DR-4 repudiation that vetoes one. It is the same artifact on both, discriminated by `decision`.

THE DISCLOSURE THAT GOVERNS EVERY LINE BELOW: ACK-1 THROUGH ACK-6 ARE NOT CLAUSES OF ZIFFER-SPEC-001. The string `ACK-` does not occur in that document at all. They are reference-level rules, written for v1.3.12 in `reference/src/acp_ack.py` to close T-31, and the two places that already say so in as many words are the leg register (`DR-9, ACK-1..6 (reference-level)`) and `spec/schemas/bundle/attesters.schema.json` (`ACK-4 (reference-level ... not a spec clause)`). ZIFFER-SPEC-001 states the OBLIGATIONS this object discharges -- DR-9 requires positive acknowledgement from at least one notified party who is not the operator, DR-4 admits repudiation from any notified party, DR-5 admits it only from a notified party and forbids the repudiation path from depending on the approval chain -- and states NOTHING about the artifact that carries them: no field list, no canonicalization, no validity bound, no identity type, no nonce type. Every field below therefore cites the reference-level ACK-* rule that put it there together with the ZIFFER-SPEC-001 clause it serves. A second implementation written from ZIFFER-SPEC-001 alone would not produce this object and would still be conformant with the document. That is the same hole ACP-87 was filed for one layer down, and it is wider here: there the type of one field was unstated, here the whole artifact is.

ONE ARTIFACT OR TWO, AND WHY THIS SCHEMA IS ONE. The leg register makes them two rows with DIFFERENT clause sets -- F5.4 carries `DR-9, ACK-1..6`, F5.5 carries only `DR-4, DR-5` and names no ACK-* rule at all. The reference makes them ONE object: there is exactly one closed field set, and `confirm()` and `repudiate()` run the identical `_verify_ack` and differ only in which value of `decision` they will accept afterwards. Read literally, the register says a repudiation must satisfy DR-4 and DR-5 and nothing else -- which is the v1.3.11 bare-name form (T-31) still standing on the veto leg, unsigned, while the confirmation leg was fixed. It does not stand in the code. The register and the reference disagree, the disagreement is recorded rather than silently resolved (that is the ACP-57 shape), and this schema follows the code because the code is what runs.

WHY THE FIELD SET IS CLOSED. ACK-1: an acknowledgement is an object with a closed schema -- exactly these fields, no optional ones, no extension point. An object carrying an unknown field or omitting a declared one MUST be rejected, never normalized and never defaulted. That is why `additionalProperties` is false at both levels and why `required` lists every property, and it is why `x-acp-absent` appears here only on the signature map: an absent-value rule on a field of a closed object would be a defect rather than a control. The reason is Z4, stated for the Attestation Object and applying unchanged here because this object is on the same binding path: given ANY optional field, the object present-as-null and the object with the field omitted are each valid canonical encodings, hash to TWO DISTINCT ids, and therefore claim TWO ledger slots. One acknowledgement, spent twice; ACK-5's single use defeated without forging anything. Canonicalization cannot fix it, because the ambiguity is in the field set rather than the encoding.

ENCODING, AND THE CLAUSE THAT IS MISSING. ACK-1 says the object is `canonically encoded` and NO clause anywhere says WHICH canonicalization. ZIFFER-SPEC-001 pins the other two: RFC 8785 (JCS) for the Proposal, canonical CBOR (RFC 8949 4.2) for the receipt and the Attestation Object (WE-1, WE-2, AT-8a). AT-8a's whole rationale is that object hashing moved onto the binding path, so any encoder disagreement between issuer and verifier becomes a freshness and single-use defect. This object is on that same path by construction: its id is a hash over its canonical encoding and the Consumption Ledger consumes that id (ACK-5). Two encoders means two ids for one acknowledgement, so a re-encoded acknowledgement claims a fresh slot and replays -- Y1b reopening in the machinery a later fix introduced, which is the RES-8/9/10 recurrence pattern this repository has now published five times. The rule AT-8a states for the Attestation Object is the rule this object needs and does not have. Filed, not invented here.

WHAT IS NOT A FIELD. The acknowledgement id. ACK-5 recomputes it as a hash over the canonical object and consumes it in the ledger; it is never transmitted and never read from the message. That is Y1b's lesson applied before it could be rediscovered, and a schema property for it would invite exactly the read that was closed as Y1. There is likewise no field naming the pending action other than `proposal_hash`, no field asserting that the acknowledger was notified (that is the Executor's own record, tested under DR-5), and no field carrying the reversibility class (RV-3: recomputed from the signed bundle, never read from a message).

SUITE 12 CLASSIFICATION. Every field here is class T at the SCHEMA layer, because a schema constrains shape and shape is not authority. What lifts them is stated on each property and enforced elsewhere: `acknowledger` becomes B once the signature over the canonical object verifies against the key the SIGNED BUNDLE registers for that name (ACK-2/ACK-4, and row 27 of the classification table records that it was T through v1.3.11 -- that was T-31); `proposal_hash` becomes B against the Executor's own recomputed hash (ACK-3); `policy_bundle_hash` and `bundle_epoch` are compared against the bundle the Executor already holds and are never used to SELECT a bundle.

WHAT THIS SCHEMA DOES NOT CONSTRAIN, STATED BEFORE ANYTHING IT DOES. (1) ORDER. The reference consumes the ledger slot inside `_verify_ack`, BEFORE the `decision`, DR-5 membership and DR-9 non-operator tests run -- so submitting a captured, validly signed REPUDIATE object to the confirmation endpoint burns its id, the genuine repudiation is then refused as a replay (CL-3), and a REVERSIBLE unsampled floor-HIGH action releases on silence under DR-7 with its veto suppressed. Executed, not reasoned about: `confirm(REPUDIATE)` refuses at ACK-1, `repudiate` then refuses at CL-3, `release` then succeeds. DR-5 exists to stop a veto being suppressed by the approval chain, and no shape constraint can express this. (2) The ACK-6 window LENGTH bound, and that the acknowledgement falls inside the hold window it is acknowledging. (3) CR-3's requirement that the signature key set exactly match the declared suite, and CR-4's containment against the bundle floor -- both are decided against the signed bundle, which a schema cannot see. (4) DR-3 delivery and DR-8 deliverability. (5) Whether any human read anything: A-8 is untouched, and acknowledgement remains an input to the model rather than evidence of comprehension.

obj.description: The signed object. Carried in its own member rather than flattened beside the signature because the id and the signature are both taken over THIS map alone (ACK-2, ACK-5): flattening would put the signature inside the bytes it signs. The reference refuses an acknowledgement with no `obj` at ACK-1 by name, because the v1.3.11 form that this member's absence identifies is a bare string -- T-31, an identity anyone could type.

sig.description:
CR-2: a signature under a suite is a MAP from primitive name to signature value, one entry per primitive of the suite named in `obj.alg`. A bare scalar signature MUST NOT be accepted under any suite, not even a single-primitive one -- format leniency is a downgrade in disguise, and the reference refuses a non-map before it looks at any value.

OPEN MAP, DELIBERATELY. The suite registry lives in the SIGNED BUNDLE (CR-1) and CR-7 makes migration forward-only, requiring a deployment to verify structures signed under a HIGHER suite than its floor. A closed `{classical, pq}` object here would hard-code one suite into the wire format and make CR-7 unimplementable; it would also be a second registry of primitive names beside the bundle's, which is the two-definitions defect.

CR-3 IS CONJUNCTIVE AND IS NOT EXPRESSIBLE HERE. Verification succeeds only if EVERY primitive of the declared suite verifies and the supplied set EXACTLY matches it -- no missing entries and no extra ones, an accepted extra primitive being an undeclared code path chosen by the party under verification. Whether this map's key set matches depends on `obj.alg` resolved against the bundle, so it is checked in code and not here.

THE VALUE TYPE IS NOT PINNED BY ANY CLAUSE, AND THE TWO IMPLEMENTATIONS OF IT DISAGREE. WE-4 pins `b64:` plus padded RFC 4648 4 base64 for `any signature or byte string carried as text`, while `reference/src/acp_executor.py` hex-encodes every signature value with the comment that signatures travel through JSON and raw bytes do not, and `spec/schemas/bundle/attesters.schema.json` carries public keys as bare base64 with no prefix at all. Three encodings of one concept in one repository. A pattern is therefore NOT asserted here, because asserting one would decide a normative question by writing a schema -- exactly what ACP-87 was filed rather than done.

additionalProperties.description: One primitive's signature value over the canonical encoding of `obj`. `minLength` only: see the encoding disagreement on the parent.

x-acp-absent.why: a primitive named by the declared suite and absent from this map is a hybrid signature verified on fewer primitives than it claims, which is the OR composition CR-3 forbids: a hybrid verifier that accepts when EITHER half checks out is weaker than its weaker member, so an attacker who breaks one primitive is unconstrained by the other. Refuse, never treat a missing primitive as satisfied and never verify the subset that is present.

acknowledgement_object.description: The signed acknowledgement object -- the bytes the signature covers and the bytes the id is derived from. ACK-1's closed field set, exactly `ACK1_FIELDS` in `reference/src/acp_ack.py`, in the order that file declares them. Adding a field here is a BREAKING change, never an additive one, for the Z4 reason on the root: a field set with an optional member gives one object two ids and two ledger slots.

proposal_hash.description:
THE BINDING, and the reason the object exists rather than a name. ACK-3: this MUST equal the hash the Executor recomputed for the action it is about to release; an acknowledgement of a different action is not an acknowledgement of this one. Without it a captured acknowledgement for a routine action is replayed onto a dangerous one, which is Y1 one layer up -- there a genuine quorum raised for P1 verified against an attacker-chosen P2.

The Executor compares against ITS OWN recomputed hash, never against a hash the same message supplied: a transmitted identifier is a name for a binding, not evidence of one (RES-8).

policy_bundle_hash.description: The signed bundle the acknowledger was acting under. ACK-3 requires it to equal the hash of the bundle the Executor holds, so an acknowledgement raised under a superseded policy cannot release an action graded under the current one. It selects nothing: the Executor already has its bundle and this value is compared to it, because a hash that chose which policy to load would let the acknowledging party choose the policy that judges them.

bundle_epoch.description: Epoch of that bundle, compared for equality by ACK-3 alongside the hash. Carried as well as the hash because the two fail differently and a reader should see which: a hash mismatch means a different bundle, an epoch mismatch means a different version of the policy basis. Epoch MONOTONICITY is not a property of this field -- it is enforced at the KMS against a durable high-water mark (RAD-3), never from a value a message carries.

acknowledger.description:
The identity acknowledging, INSIDE the signature. ACK-4 is the whole of T-31's lesson: the identity used for the DR-9 non-operator test and the DR-5 notified-membership test is taken FROM THE SIGNED BYTES, never from the call that delivered the object. Through v1.3.11 it was a bare string checked only for set membership and inequality with the operator -- the release gate held no key material at all, and an irreversible action released with `human_verified` true and zero signatures verified.

ACK-2 makes the name resolvable rather than authoritative: it selects a key from the attester registry inside the SIGNED bundle, and an identity with no registered key cannot acknowledge anything. The signature establishes who signed; this field only says which enrolled key to check it against. It does not authorise anyone to name themselves.

BOUNDED AT 128 BECAUSE THE REGISTRY IT MUST RESOLVE IN IS. `spec/schemas/bundle/attesters.schema.json` bounds its `propertyNames` at 1..128, so a longer value cannot name an enrolled attester and the same bound belongs on both sides of the lookup. It is also the bound `AttestationObject.operator` carries, which matters because DR-9 compares this value to that one: two bounds on one identity space would make a name that is a valid acknowledger and an invalid operator, and the non-operator test compares them.

decision.description:
Which of the two acts this object is: CONFIRM is the DR-9 positive acknowledgement that permits an IRREVERSIBLE floor-HIGH action to release; REPUDIATE is the DR-4 veto that blocks release with a critical alert and requires a fresh quorum rather than a replay.

HOISTED INTO $defs rather than written inline for the reason `attester_role` gives in the bundle schemas: an inline enum has no name, and a generator inventing one invents a name that drifts.

DELIBERATELY NOT ORDERED. A repudiation does not outrank a confirmation on some scale; they are different acts with different consequences, and DR-4's precedence -- a repudiated action fails closed at release however many confirmations it also collected -- is enforced in the release step against `repudiated_by`, not by comparing two enum members.

THIS FIELD IS INSIDE THE SIGNATURE, AND THAT IS THE POINT. It is the discriminator between the two legs, so an attacker who could rewrite it would turn a veto into an approval. Being an ACK-1 field it is signature-covered, exactly as CR-5 requires of `alg` and AT-1 of `operator` after Y4. A verifier MUST still check it against the endpoint that received the object: a valid REPUDIATE object is not a confirmation merely because it was posted to the confirmation path.

ack_nonce.description:
Freshness material, so that two acknowledgements of the same action under the same bundle by the same party are distinct objects with distinct ids. ACK-5 consumes the derived id in the ledger, so this is what stops a second honest acknowledgement colliding with the first.

ITS TYPE AND ITS ENTROPY ARE UNSTATED, AND THE REFERENCE MAKES IT PREDICTABLE. AT-1 requires a 128-bit FRESH nonce for the Attestation Object and WE-4 pins that value's wire type; no clause says anything about this one, and `make_ack` builds it as the acknowledger's own name joined to a millisecond timestamp (observed: `ack-op_1121-1787598182147`). It is therefore neither random nor unique -- two acknowledgements by one party in one millisecond collide -- and, because every other field of the object is already known to the operator, the derived ledger id is guessable to within the timestamp resolution. The ledger id is the single-use key, so a guessed id can be claimed before the honest acknowledgement arrives, and the honest one is then refused as a replay.

`minLength: 1` and nothing more, deliberately. A zero-length nonce contributes no freshness at all, which is a shape claim a schema may make; a length or an alphabet would be this schema inventing the normative rule that is missing, and inventing it here is how a type comes to exist in a schema and nowhere else -- the defect the sibling wire schema records against its own `att_nonce`.

issued_at.description:
When the acknowledgement was raised, in seconds since the Unix epoch. ACK-6 requires `issued_at <= now <= expires_at` at the consumer, evaluated against NTS-disciplined wall time within the L-20 skew allowance (leg F9.1 carries that dependency).

THIS IS THE ONE STRUCTURE IN THE WIRE FORMAT WHOSE TIMES ARE NUMBERS, AND THE REFERENCE PUTS FLOATS IN IT. Section 9.2's receipt and AT-1's `expires_at` are RFC 3339 strings; only the acknowledgement is numeric, and `make_ack` defaults to `time.time()`, so a float reaches the canonical bytes on every production path. AT-8a forbids a float in a canonical structure because a float is not deterministically encoded, and `canon()` enforces that only at the top level -- a nested float is serialised, observed as `{"ack_nonce":...,"issued_at":1787598182.1470501,...}`. Two runtimes formatting that value differently derive two ids for one acknowledgement, which is precisely the encoding split AT-8a exists to prevent and precisely the ledger-slot defect Y1b closed.

`integer` is pinned here because it is the only one of the three encodings present in this repository -- float, integer, RFC 3339 -- that AT-8a permits. Which of the remaining two the acknowledgement SHOULD carry is a normative question ZIFFER-SPEC-001 does not answer, and pinning the narrower of what exists is not the same as answering it.

expires_at.description:
When the acknowledgement stops being valid, in seconds since the Unix epoch, on the same clock and with the same float caveat as `issued_at`.

THE WINDOW LENGTH IS ENFORCED BY THE CONSUMER, NOT READ FROM THE MESSAGE. ACK-6 requires `expires_at - issued_at` to be bounded, and that bound is checked by the Executor -- the Y2 lesson, where receipt validity LENGTH was checked nowhere and lived only in the value the signing party wrote, permitting long-lived pre-positioned receipts. A schema cannot express a relation between two fields, so this constraint is stated and not asserted.

THE BOUND ITSELF HAS NO CLAUSE. The reference uses 120 seconds and its comment says the figure mirrors L-14 -- but L-14 is the ALLOW receipt validity ceiling, a limit on a different artifact with a different lifetime, and the section 13 limits table has no row for an acknowledgement window. A borrowed number is not a normative bound; recorded rather than restated as one.

alg.description:
The signature suite `sig` is under. CR-1: every signed structure MUST carry an explicit `alg` naming a suite REGISTERED IN THE SIGNED BUNDLE, and an unregistered or unknown suite MUST fail closed. CR-5: it is signature-covered, so an issuer cannot rewrite the suite without invalidating the object -- an acknowledger cannot downgrade its own suite.

NO ENUM, DELIBERATELY. The suite set is a bundle property, so an enum here would be a second registry of suite names beside the signed one, and two definitions of one object is the defect this repository is built around. It would also break CR-7, which makes migration forward-only and requires a deployment to verify structures signed under a suite HIGHER than its floor: a suite the schema had not been updated to list would be refused at the wrong layer, for the wrong reason, with the wrong clause name.

CR-4 IS CONTAINMENT AND IS DECIDED AGAINST THE BUNDLE. The floor is satisfied when the named suite's primitive set CONTAINS every primitive of the bundle floor's suite -- not by rank. The rank table this replaced was a total order over sets that are not comparable, and it let a deployment whose signed floor said hash-based post-quantum silently accept a lattice one: not a stronger suite accepted, a DIFFERENT hardness assumption substituted, with the floor check reporting satisfaction. The reference checks the floor BEFORE verifying the signature, so a below-floor acknowledgement refuses at CR-4 rather than at ACK-2.

ack_decision.description: The two acts an acknowledgement can be. Closed enum: the reference refuses any other value at ACK-1 by name, before the signature is checked, because a third value would be an act with no defined consequence and the release path would have to guess at it.
